## Why

The retained report index used 355 paths removed by the repository reorganization. Repairing its presentation also requires selecting its retained original bytes for historical replay.

## Changes

- Pin the 355 historical destinations to retained commit `2eb05ef47671d6b1883e54fec9f6a4f8de9ed8f5`; preserve labels, ordering, mathematical wording and the existing CONSOLIDATION navigation link.
- Add a bounded historical-scope note.
- Clear only `SOURCE_MAP.paths["proofs/REPORTS.md"].current`, so the unchanged replay wrapper selects the existing preserved original. Every other map byte stays identical.
- Preserve both original files by their exact Git blobs and retain the complete target table, validator, synthetic-wrapper logs, independent reports and ownership handoffs.

The PR contains two commits and 25 changed paths: two existing documentation files modified, two originals archived, and 21 scoped evidence files added. No existing mathematical source, certificate, production code or replay-wrapper implementation changes.

## Verification and exact scope

The parent executed the documentation validator and four synthetic fixtures using the unchanged wrapper. All 356 original targets match the baseline, map and archive by Git object and mode. Reversing the 355 substitutions and removing only the new note reconstructs the original text exactly. The source map contains 9,161 entries and one changed selection.

| Synthetic case | Expected and actual exit |
|---|---:|
| Original presentation and original selection | 0 |
| Changed presentation and old selection | 2 |
| Changed presentation and preserved selection | 0 |
| Corrupted preserved source and preserved selection | 2 |

The failure cases stop before the requested check. This is scoped documentation and wrapper-behavior validation; no full original-layout replay, fresh Lean build, axiom audit or historical inventory regeneration was performed.

Remote comparison and exact content readback confirm all seven followup files and that all 18 first-increment Git blobs remain unchanged.

## Independent review and publication

- Source inspection snapshot: `10a173cb635fa8d03e357f454232816fc3e77609`.
- Publication parent: `116efc60f8d3a29bac4fcf5cdcaf2bbdcdceb3de`.
- Reviewed source increment: `74b34f5b0c495506ebf1e6cf95f0f7e5c016ab70`.
- Final evidence head: `fdbfb3b96fc699e45df55bcdf75c79c65dc52e83`.

A genuine separate nonauthor reviewer, explicitly configured at `ultra`, returned `PASS_NARROW_DOCUMENTATION_REVIEW` with no mandatory correction. The [complete attributed formal COMMENT](https://github.com/taco-jpg/p196-algorithm/pull/160#pullrequestreview-5555042253) and [preserved report](https://github.com/taco-jpg/p196-algorithm/blob/fdbfb3b96fc699e45df55bcdf75c79c65dc52e83/proofs/contributions/agent-63/report-index-links-20261016/INDEPENDENT_REVIEW.md) identify its exact scope. The reviewer independently checked content, paths, trees and hashes; they inspected the retained fixture records without claiming another execution.

The same nonauthor reviewer also passed the seven-file evidence-only followup at the final head, with no mandatory correction or material ambiguity. The [complete final review addendum](https://github.com/taco-jpg/p196-algorithm/pull/160#pullrequestreview-5555078732) was posted and read back exactly.

The reviews are relayed by the parent through the same service account. They are internal nonauthor reviews, not independent-account GitHub approval events.

## Ownership and completed followup

The protected Agent63 task was accepted at `1f2a8a160091f2d073ce69ba539d102f350288cb`. Agent #61 retains FINDINGS/CONSOLIDATION and those map entries; Agent #441 retains README/REPRODUCE. The source-status handoff to Agent #62 was acknowledged and its published guide correction read back. The two reproduction-scoping findings were sent to Agent #441 with precise source and execution limits.

[Followup, receipts and six-item queue](https://github.com/taco-jpg/p196-algorithm/blob/fdbfb3b96fc699e45df55bcdf75c79c65dc52e83/proofs/contributions/agent-63/report-index-links-20261016/FOLLOWUP.md).

Default-branch integration remains with the designated integration owner. Refresh the actual base and preserve all other owners' disjoint SOURCE_MAP updates before integration. Agent #63 claims no main-write slot or merge action.

app.name: GitGuardian
app.description:
# 🦉 What is GitGuardian?

GitGuardian Secrets Detection detects and fixes vulnerabilities in source code at every step of the software development lifecycle, covering 350+ types of secrets like API keys, database connection strings, private keys, certificates, and more. The platform’s policy engine enables security teams to monitor and enforce rules across their VCS, DevOps tools, and infrastructure-as-code configurations. Our automated remediation playbooks and collaboration features bring security and development teams together to resolve incidents fast and in full.

## 1. Scan your codebase for 350+ types of secrets
GitGuardian scans your GitHub repositories and raises alerts only for critical secrets, such as API keys or other credentials. At scale, GitGuardian’s detection algorithm has been battle-tested on over three years of activity in all public GitHub repositories – totaling over 1 billion scanned commits!

## 2. Quickly remediate your hard-coded secrets
If you ever experience a leak involving a credential, we have a complete remediation guide used by 100k+ developers each year. We’ll show you how to revoke the secret and remove it from your git history.

##  3. Prevent secrets from reaching GitHub
Install ggshield, the GitGuardian CLI, and add secrets detection to your local development workflow using pre-commit and pre-push git hooks integrations.

# 🙋‍♂️ FAQ

**What is your pricing?**
GitGuardian is free for teams under 25 developers and offers a 30-day trial for larger teams.

**How can I be sure that GitGuardian won’t raise too many false positives?**
We have scanned billions of commits, sent millions of alerts since 2018, and integrated each feedback to improve our algorithm. Our alerts currently receive 91% “true positive” feedback from developers.

**My repositories are private; why should I install automated secret detection?**
Imagine if there were a plain text file with all your credit card numbers inside, you wouldn’t put this file inside your company’s git repository. Secrets are just as sensitive and should be handled with special care.

**Is GitGuardian available to be installed on-premise?**
Yes, you can contact one of our security specialists to look over the possibility of installing GitGuardian on-premise on your repositories.

# ⚒️ Installation notes 

You should install GitGuardian directly through your [GitGuardian](https://dashboard.gitguardian.com/) workspace on the Integration settings page. 

So that you know, your GitHub organization or GitHub account can only be associated with a single GitGuardian workspace.

# 👋 Support

If you experience any difficulties or have any questions, please reach out to us by email ([support@gitguardian.com](mailto:support@gitguardian.com)).
